reason: The narration describes three distinct visual states: the head lying in the earth for two and a half millennia, then standing as a scarecrow on a yam patch for a year, and finally being recognized in hands. Each state requires a separate visual to match the semantic shift in location, function, and perception.

beats.visual_intent: A terracotta head lying in soil, buried and undisturbed, in a rural field or garden setting in central Nigeria, with surrounding vegetation and earth showing age and decay.
search_queries: terracotta head buried in soil central Nigeria
ancient terracotta figure in earth archaeological site
requirements: setting is rural, in central Nigeria
context shows age and natural decay
avoid: head being handled or visible above ground
beats.edit: Slow, steady shot of the head in soil, with subtle environmental details like roots or soil erosion to imply time passage.

beats.visual_intent: The same terracotta head placed as a scarecrow on a patch of land growing yams, with yam plants visible and the head partially exposed, standing still in a rural field.
search_queries: terracotta scarecrow on yam patch Nigeria
ancient terracotta figure as scarecrow in field
terracotta head on yam garden central Nigeria
requirements: head is positioned as a scarecrow
head is not buried, but upright
avoid: modern farm equipment or people present
beats.edit: Medium shot showing the head as a scarecrow, with yam plants in background, emphasizing stillness and rural life.

beats.visual_intent: A person's hand reaching toward or holding the terracotta head, with the head visible in their grip, in a rural setting in central Nigeria, suggesting recognition and surprise.
search_queries: person picking up ancient terracotta sculpture
requirements: a person's hand is visible holding the head
avoid: no person present or hand visible
beats.edit: Close-up of hand gently lifting or holding the head, with soft lighting and background showing rural context to emphasize the moment of realization.
